selected.title: Major share market float of Firmus in trouble as interest wanes
selected.summary: The company is reportedly having to price its shares lower as it closed its books to potential investors abruptly overnight.
selected.why: Abrupt bookbuild closure and forced repricing mark an unexpected IPO stumble.

Its data centres require a lot of energy and expansion plans have been described as ambitious. ( Supplied: Tasmanian government ) In short: The $44 billion Australian float of data centre operator Firmus appears to be in trouble. But Firmus is not currently listed on the ASX's "upcoming floats and listings" webpage, and analysts who spoke to the ABC have raised concerns over the firm’s debts and the wild increase in its valuation over a short period of time. What's next? The company is scheduled to float on the ASX on October 23. abc.net.au/news/firmus-ipo-underwhelms-before-it-hits-the-market/107241548 Link copied Share Share article It was touted as the biggest float since Telstra in the 1990s, but the share market debut of data centre operator Firmus is in trouble before it has even hit the share market. Investment banks stopped taking bids for the initial public offering (IPO) today and will now determine at what price the company lists on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX). But Firmus is not currently listed on the ASX's "upcoming floats and listings" webpage, and analysts who spoke to the ABC have raised concerns over the firm's debts and the wild increase in its valuation over a short period of time. Adding to concerns, Goldman Sachs was reportedly tapped to rescue the float from collapse at midday today. The ABC has contacted several industry players directly connected with Firmus's fundraising, including Wilson Asset Management, Bank of America and Goldman Sachs. The investment bank told the ABC it had no comment. Fund manager Roger Montgomery said there had been inconsistencies in the messages given to market participants about the capital raising.
